title: docs(manifest-snippets): declare the elision in five defineStack manifest examples
body:
Fixes #18777

## What changed

Five `defineStack({ manifest: … })` documentation snippets carried an **incomplete manifest
literal with no elision marker**, so a reader copying the block is refused at
`ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`. Seven sibling snippets in the same corpora already declare
their elision; these five were silent. This PR makes the elision explicit at all five,
in a form that already exists in this tree.

| site | manifest keys (unchanged by this PR) | elision marker: before / after |
|---|---|---|
| `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx` | `id`, `namespace` | none / present |
| `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` | `namespace` | none / present |
| `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx` | `name`, `namespace`, `version` | none / present |
| `content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx` | `name`, `version` | none / present |
| `docs/design/marketplace-publishing.md` | `id`, `type`, `namespace`, `version` | none / present |

The seven sites that already carry a marker are **not touched** — the card explicitly does
not assert that they need anything.

## Which existing form, and why

Re-measured over the seven sibling sites on `objectstack-ai/objectstack` @ `ad1f94e8e`
(this branch's base). The dispatch's 3 / 3 / 1 count is **confirmed exactly**:

| form | spelling | count | sites |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | inline, Unicode ellipsis — `manifest: { /* … */ },` | 3 | `protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`, `data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx`, `data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx` |
| B | inline, ASCII three dots — `manifest: { /* ... */ },` | 3 | `deployment/cli.mdx`, `plugins/index.mdx`, `packages/mcp/README.md` |
| C | multi-line: real keys kept, elision comment on its own line | 1 | `packages/services/service-package/README.md` |

**Form C is used at all five sites.** One reason, and it is the same at every site: Form C
is the only one of the three that is **additive**. Forms A and B replace the literal's
contents, which would delete the very keys each of these five snippets exists to
demonstrate — `authorization.mdx` is teaching `namespace`, `capabilities.mdx` is teaching
the `name`/`namespace`/`version` triple next to a capability declaration,
`record-view-auditing.mdx` is teaching a stack that names itself while opting into the
audit plugin, and `marketplace-publishing.md`'s prose one paragraph above says
"Compose all internal plugins into a single `type: 'app'` package", which is the `type` key
in that literal. A snippet that loses its subject to gain a marker is worse at its job.

No fourth form was invented: the comment text is `/* …full ObjectStackManifest… */`, byte
for byte the one Form C's site already uses.

Proof the edit is purely additive — the post-change literal was extracted from each file by
brace matching, evaluated as JS, and its key list read back:

```text
content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx         keys after edit : ["id","namespace"]
content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx         keys after edit : ["namespace"]
content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx          keys after edit : ["name","namespace","version"]
content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx  keys after edit : ["name","version"]
docs/design/marketplace-publishing.md              keys after edit : ["id","type","namespace","version"]
```

Identical to the before-lists in the card's table. No key was added, removed or reworded.

## Premise re-taken at the real door

Each literal driven through `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` from the built
`packages/spec/dist/index.mjs` (spec built at this branch's base):

```text
REFUSED  content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx
         invalid_type[manifest,version] · invalid_value[manifest,type] · invalid_type[manifest,name]
REFUSED  content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx
         invalid_type[manifest,id] · invalid_type[manifest,version] · invalid_value[manifest,type] · invalid_type[manifest,name]
REFUSED  content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx
         invalid_type[manifest,id] · invalid_value[manifest,type]
REFUSED  content/docs/permissions/record-view-auditing.mdx
         invalid_type[manifest,id] · invalid_value[manifest,type]
REFUSED  docs/design/marketplace-publishing.md
         invalid_type[manifest,name]
POSITIVE CONTROL (complete manifest): ACCEPTED
```

Row for row identical to the card's table, and the card's correction holds: the `/* … */`
on the same line as the fifth site's manifest sits in **`plugins:`**, not in `manifest:`.

## Read this before reviewing: what this PR does NOT do

**An elision marker is a comment. It does not make any of these five snippets parse.** The
same door, driven against the post-change literals, returns the same refusal codes at all
five sites. What changes is the snippet's *status*: a silent omission becomes a declared
partial, which is the boundary #18776 drew when it judged `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx`
"incomplete, not an error" because its elision was written down.

That is the remedy the card's triage chose, of the two the card offered. If the intent was
instead that a reader can copy any of these five blocks and have it run, that is the card's
other arm — completing each manifest to `id` + `name` + `type` + `version` — and this PR is
not it. Reviewer's call; the measurement above is the same either way.

## Corpus-wide closing measurement

Every `manifest: {` literal in the prose corpora (`content/**`, `docs/**`, every
`README.md`, `skills/**`, `examples/**`; CHANGELOGs excluded) was brace-matched, evaluated
and driven at the same door — 44 literals across 1224 files. After this change:

- 24 accepted at the door;
- 13 refused **with** a declared elision — the 7 siblings, the 5 in this PR, and
  `content/docs/upgrading.mdx:156`, which declares its elision with a `// ...` line comment;
- 2 refused **without** one, both in `.changeset/*.md` release-note prose, which is a
  fragment describing a diff rather than a copyable stack config and is consumed at release.

So the class this card names is empty on the published docs surface after this PR. That
`// ...` line-comment spelling at `upgrading.mdx:156` is a **fourth** elision spelling in the
corpus; it is reported, not changed — the site is a manifest fragment, not a `defineStack`
call, and the card asserts nothing about already-declared partials.

## Verification

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives
**43 commands** from this change set (5 paths, merge base `ad1f94e8e`). All 43 were run:

- **39 exit 0.**
- **4 refused on an unmet prerequisite, then re-run green after building what they named**
  (`check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:doc-security-posture`, `check:docs-transcript-drift`,
  `check:skill-examples`).

`pnpm lint` is not implicated, and this is a measurement rather than a skipped step:
eslint's own population, read from `eslint.config.mjs`, is
`**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` and narrower subsets of it — the string `mdx` does
not occur in that file, and no block names `.md`. Running eslint over the five changed files
with `--format json` returns 5 results, every one of them
`File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied`, 0 errors, 0 warnings other
than that notice, exit 0. Type-aware linting is not enabled for this diff's file kinds, so
no untouched file's verdict can move.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset`: nothing published moves. All five edited paths sit at the repository root
(`content/docs/**`, `docs/design/**`), outside every workspace package directory, and the
root package is `private: true` — an npm tarball can only contain files under its own
package directory, so no `files[]` entry in this repo can reach them. Positive control, same
method: `packages/services/service-package/README.md` (the untouched Form C sibling, the same
kind of prose) **does** ship, as a README of a published package, and
`packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts` ships too — `npm pack --dry-run` in
`packages/spec` lists `44.3kB src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts` in the tarball contents.

## Acceptance notes

Findings noted while working, none filed:

- The corpus carries **two inline spellings of the same inline elision** — three sites with
  the Unicode ellipsis `/* … */` and three with the ASCII `/* ... */` — plus the multi-line
  Form C and the `// ...` line comment at `upgrading.mdx:156`. Four spellings of one idea.
  Noted, not filed: this is a consistency observation, not a reproducible defect, and the
  card explicitly does not assert that already-declared partials need anything.
- `packages/services/service-package/README.md`'s own manifest literal (Form C's site) is
  refused at the door too — `invalid_value[manifest,type]`. Noted, not filed: it is a
  declared partial, which is precisely the disposition this card adopts.
